published_statement: EHLS 1110.2087v2 Def.3 (pp.5-6): 'If (M, g, k) is asymptotically flat, one can define the ADM energy E and the ADM momentum P as E = 1/(2(n-1)omega_{n-1}) lim_{r->inf} int_{|x|=r} sum_{i,j} (g_ij,i - g_ii,j) nu^j_0 dH^{n-1}_0 ... Here, the integrals are computed in the coordinate chart M \ K ~ R^n \ B, nu^j_0 = x^j/|x| ...'. McCormick 2401.05128v1 Def.2.2 (p.5): the same flux, with 'By the work of Bartnik [10] and Chrusciel [26] it is now well-known that the ADM mass is well-defined and independent of the diffeomorphism phi used to define it.' For n = 3 the normalisation is 1/(16 pi); for g_ij = (1 - 2 Phi) delta_ij this is E = lim r^2 Phi'(r) (derived here, C1), so E is the coefficient of the 1/r tail of Phi exactly when the SPATIAL metric carries the same Phi as g_tt.
published_hypotheses: H1 an asymptotically flat end: a compact K and a chart M \ K ~ R^3 \ B in which g - delta = O(|x|^-tau), d g = O(|x|^-tau-1), d^2 g = O(|x|^-tau-2), tau > (n-2)/2 = 1/2 (McCormick Def.2.1; EHLS Def.3 in weighted Sobolev form, q in (1/2, 1) for n = 3)
H2 finiteness needs integrable scalar curvature in addition to H1 (McCormick p.5); coordinate independence under H1+H2 is Bartnik 1986 / Chrusciel 1986 (NAMED-NOT-READ, restated by McCormick)
H3 E is a flux of the SPATIAL metric g_ij on a slice -- not of g_tt; the Newtonian identification 'E = coefficient of 1/r in Phi' holds when g_ij = (1 - 2 Phi) delta_ij + o(1/r) (derived here, C1-C2)

H4 the definition is kinematic: no field equation or energy condition enters; the mass it assigns includes gravitational binding energy (ADM shell self-energy, restated by Dillon 1303.2706 eqs (2),(7))
H5 regularity inside K is irrelevant to the definition (only the end matters); EHLS's C^2_loc completeness is for their theorem, not for E

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result: the ADM mass is a DEFINITION with no empirical input, so there is no datum ADM (1959-62) could have lacked that moves it. What came later was rigour, not data: Bartnik and Chrusciel (1986) supplied the fall-off (tau > 1/2) and integrable-scalar-curvature hypotheses under which the flux is finite and chart-independent. Evidence that this later knowledge does NOT move the tree's use: the tree's metric decays as r^-3 (C3), far inside the window, so the flux is unambiguous and equals 0 exactly. Evidence that it DOES narrow the use, but through the tree's own hypotheses and not through missing data: (i) ADM's own shell result (via Dillon) already says the ADM mass counts binding energy, so 'monopoles of -m and +m cancel' is a first-order statement -- the tree's linearisation (named at concentric.py:139-141) reaches M_ADM = 0 at the matter level, which the tree says it does not (concentric.py:37-38); (ii) stability.py's flat exterior needs a compactly supported core, which the Plummer core is not (1.5e-8 effect). Neither is a failure of the external result. Verdict on M's hypothesis for this entry: evidence against -- the external definition is accurate and complete for this use.
grade_evidence: The external definition STANDS as the tree applies it to its metric: read in two exact restatements (EHLS Def.3; McCormick Def.2.2), re-derived symbolically (C1-C2), and the tree's M_ADM = 0 is exactly zero for the metric it writes, with r^-3 decay (C3). No moved datum. The grade is NARROWED, not STANDS, because the tree uses it on a larger class than the hypotheses support, in two places: (1) stability.py:16-19 drops the vacuum-exterior / compact-support hypothesis that 'M_ADM = 0 => flat Minkowski exterior' needs (Birkhoff); the Plummer core leaves 1.5e-8 m outside R_s (C6) -- numerically negligible, a named-hypothesis omission; (2) concentric.py:37-38, 49-50 treat 'monopoles cancel => M_ADM = 0 EXACTLY' as untouched by linearisation, but the ADM mass counts binding (H4), so the matter-level identification holds to first order in m/a; post-linear estimate -7.4 % of m at the design point (C8, an estimate). Not WRONG: no counterexample to anything the tree computes; the metric-level zero is exact, and stability.py's own junction keeps M_out = 0 exactly by tuning the shell (C7). Separately recorded as a DISCREPANCY, not a refutation: concentric.py:50-51's printed Phi(1000) = -6.2e-13 and Phi(1) = +4.4e-3 are the a = 0.5 values, not the file's a = 0.02 values (-1.0e-15, +4.974e-3); the conclusion is unaffected. Scope of the grade: it grades the result AS THE TREE USES IT. The external definition itself (ADM flux of g_ij at spatial infinity, under tau > 1/2 decay and integrable scalar curvature) is not narrowed, contradicted or data-dependent by anything found here; M's hypothesis of missing data finds no purchase on a definition with no empirical input.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owners name (a) the isotropic-form condition Psi = Phi behind 'monopole of Phi = ADM mass', (b) a truncated/compactly supported core (or the 1.5e-8 tail) in stability.py:16-19, and (c) that 'M_ADM = 0 EXACTLY' is metric-level, first-order at the matter level (or show, by a strong-field solution, that the shell can be retuned to keep E = 0 at m/a ~ 0.25-1). To WRONG: only a demonstration that the tree's written metric has a nonzero flux, which C3 rules out analytically. To OPEN: none -- the definition is checkable here and was checked; a later read of ADM 1962 at source (gr-qc/0405109, blocked this stage by quota and proxy) would upgrade the read_status, not the grade, unless its normalisation differed from EHLS/McCormick (C2 shows the EHLS normalisation returns the Schwarzschild M).
